page: Amazon Web Services c6a.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs allocated from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2985.49, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, scoring the same 2985.49 (bottom 25%) due to the 2-vCPU limitation. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with cached small-block read bandwidth at 141.64 GB/sec (bottom 10%) and large-block write bandwidth at 21.1 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while multi-core Geekbench and software compilation tasks score in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6a.large offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources at a low entry point, though it is constrained by its 4.0 GB memory capacity and lack of local storage. This resource density makes it suitable for lightweight, compute-bound workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have low memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing. It is less suitable for database operations, software compilation, or memory-intensive applications due to poor memory and database benchmark scores.
